Record Class GTNetProtocolDescriptorDTO

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
grafiosch.gtnet.GTNetProtocolDescriptorDTO
Record Components:
name - the enum constant name, which is also the NLS key the client renders
value - the wire value, which is what a stored message row carries
category - REQUEST, RESPONSE or ANNOUNCEMENT
userInitiable - an administrator may send this code
requiresResponse - a sent instance stays open until one of its answers arrives
validResponses - the names of the codes that answer this one
hasModel - the code carries a payload
formEligible - the payload is filled in by the user, so /msgformdefinition describes it
threadable - the code may carry a replyTo without being an answer, as an admin message does
autoAnswerRequest - the code may be the request of an auto-answer rule
autoAnswerResponse - the code may be the answer of an auto-answer rule
public record GTNetProtocolDescriptorDTO(String name, byte value, MessageCategory category, boolean userInitiable, boolean requiresResponse, List<String> validResponses, boolean hasModel, boolean formEligible, boolean threadable, boolean autoAnswerRequest, boolean autoAnswerResponse) extends Record
What the client is told about one message code.

The browser used to keep its own copies of this — a response map next to the message enum, a second one next to the auto-answer rule model, and a list of the codes that may carry an auto-answer rule. All three had drifted from the server and from each other: one offered a reply the backend refuses, another omitted every application code. The client now receives the protocol instead of restating it.
